questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to ﬁll in the blank.

The company ______ its ﬁrst all-electric car in the Indian market soon.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 3.

Here, the sentence is in the present sentence. So, 'is launching', which is present continuous tense, is the most appropriate word to ﬁll in the blank.

The blank must have a present continuous tense because the action is still going on.

__Complete sentence:__ *The company **is launching** its ﬁrst all-electric car in the Indian market soon.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

The government __is set__ strict limits on public spending this year.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

Has/have/had are used alongside pronouns or nouns. 

Here, "Government' is a singular noun in the given context. So, it should be followed by *has*.

__Correct sentence:__ *The government **has set** strict limits on public spending this year.*

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 4.

'from its' is grammatically wrong because 'from' is used to indicate the point in space at which a journey, motion, or action starts.

Here, instead of 'from', 'for' should be used. 

__Correct sentence:__ *The city of Banaras is widely known **for **its ghats and temples.*

questions.question:
**Select the antonym of the given word.**

Fragile
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Tough**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The word ‘**Fragile**’(adjective) means- "easily damaged or broken". (सहज क्षतिग्रस्‍त होने या टूट जाने वाला; भंगुर)

 
 
• E.g.* Some of the more **fragile **items are kept in a locked case.*
 
 *​*Let’s have a look at the meaning of the words that are given in the options:

 
 
• **Gross**(adjective)- “being the total amount before anything is taken away”. (कुल राशि जिसमें से कुछ घटाया नहीं गया)
 
• **Novel**(adjective)- “new and different”. (नया और भिन्‍न)
 
• **Tiny**(adjective)- “very small”. (बहुत छोटा; नन्‍हा)
 
• **Tough**(adjective)- “not easily broken, torn or cut; very strong”. (आसानी से न टूटने, फटने या कटने वाला; बहुत मज़बूत)
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that ‘Tough’ is the correct antonym for the given bold word.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• *​*The antonyms of the given word 'Fragile' are- 'Tough', '**robust**', '**strong**', 'hard', '**firm**', etc.
 
• The synonyms of the given word 'Fragile' are- '**brittle**', '**feeble**', '**weak**', '**crisp**', etc.
 
• Example of 'Fragile' in a sentence__: 
 
 
• *He looked rather **fragile **after his operation.*

questions.question:

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

They won’t commit __themselves until__ they see which way the wind is blowing.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Reflexive pronouns are words like myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves and themselves.
 
• They refer back to a person or thing.
 
• We often use reflexive pronouns when the subject and the object of a verb are the same. 
 
 
• Example:* I cut myself when I was making dinner last night.*
 
 
 
• ​As the subject 'they' is plural, the reflexive pronoun must be plural.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is 'themselves.
 
• Use of until is correct. Until as a preposition means ‘up to (the time that)’

The given sentence is grammatically correct. So, no substitutions are needed. 

Rest all options are grammatically wrong.

questions.question:
**Select the synonym of the given word.**

Awkward
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Clumsy**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​​​The word ‘**Awkward**’(adjective) means- "difficult to deal with". (निपटने में मुश्किल, कठिन, कष्‍टकर)

 
 
• E.g:* It's an **awkward **corner, so take it slowly.*
 
 
 
• *​*Let’s have a look at the meaning of the words that are given in the options:
 
 
• **Worthy**(adjective)- “good enough for something or to have something”. (किसी बात या वस्‍तु या कुछ धारण करने के योग्‍य)
 
• **Likable**(adjective)- “used about a person easy to like; pleasant”. (व्‍यक्ति जो तुरंत पसंद आ जाए; आकर्षक, मनोहर)
 
• **Scared**(adjective)- “frightened”. (भयभीत)
 
• **Clumsy**(adjective)- “large, difficult to use, and not attractive in design”. (बड़ा, असुविधाजनक और बेढंगा)
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that ‘Clumsy’ is the correct synonym for the given bold word.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• *It was an **awkward **ascent, but we reached the top eventually.*

questions.question:
**Select the antonym of the given word.**

Persuade
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Dissuade**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The word ‘**Persuade**’(verb) means- "to make somebody do something by giving him/her good reasons". (समझा-बुझाकर किसी को काम के लिए राज़ी करना, मनाना)

 
 
• E.g.* If she doesn't want to go, nothing you can say will **persuade **her.**​*
 
 
 
• *​*Let’s have a look at the meaning of the words that are given in the options:
 
 
• **Endorse**(verb)- “to say publicly that you give official support or agreement to a plan, statement, decision, etc.”. (किसी योजना घोषणा, निर्णय आदि का सार्वजनिक तौर पर या अधिकृत रूप से समर्थन करना)
 
• **Dissuade**(verb)- “to persuade somebody not to do something”. (किसी को कोई काम करने से मना करना, रोकना)
 
• **Convince**(verb)- “to succeed in making somebody believe something”. (किसी को विश्‍वास दिलाना; आश्‍वस्‍त करना)
 
• **Fume**(verb)- “to be very angry about something”. (किसी बात पर बहुत क्रुद्घ होना)
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that ‘Dissuade’ is the correct antonym for the given bold word.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• *​*The antonyms of the given word 'Persuade' are- 'Dissuade', '**deter**', '**discourage**', '**prevent**', '**hinder**', etc.
 
• The synonyms of the given word 'Persuade' are- '**convince**', '**prompt**', '**procure**', '**influence**', etc.
 
• Example of 'Persuade' in a sentence__: 
 
 
• *She used her womanly charms to **persuade **him to change his mind.*
